Unfortunately, we didn't have much to choose from this time around in the race for the Governor's mansion. It came down to this clown, and a dues-paying member of the religious right.... and we wound up with this clown!.

I seriously doubt that there will be any effect at all from any of these so-called "common sense" measures. The one-gun-a-month limit does precisely nothing. The only thing that it accomplishes is it effectively stops gun collectors from purchasing entire collections, or from purchasing "matched sets" of rare firearms. Hardly the sweeping anti-gun violence move that it's being sold as.

Revoking concealed-carry permits for "deadbeat dads" is just grasping at straws. It's a way to slightly shrink to number of concealed-carriers that "reasonable people" wouldn't argue against. A prohibition on gun ownership by persons subject to protective order....meh. It's already a problem to buy one if you are the subject of a protective order, I guess they figured on taking it one more step.

The really amusing part is the bit about background checks at gun shows. I've been to more than a few. Licensed dealers already do background checks...it's the law. What this does is it requires a background check on person-to-person sales, but only at gun shows. The question is: what's the point? Criminals, by-and-large, don't go to gun shows. Too many cops at gun shows. Don't believe me? Go to a gun show in Virginia. To get in, you have to run the gauntlet of local cops that are at the entrance checking guns that are entering the show. Once you are inside the show, guess what? You are shoulder-to-shoulder with local cops, state police, and FBI agents. So why do so many law enforcement personnel go to gun shows? Because they are looking for deals on guns too!
